answer:
The scientist at MIT who won the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering in 2013 was **Sir Tim Berners-Lee**. His father was **Conway Berners-Lee** (full name: Conway Maurice Berners-Lee), a distinguished English mathematician and computer scientist who worked on some of the earliest computers, including the Ferranti Mark 1—the world's first commercial stored-program electronic computer.

Conway Berners-Lee lived from September 19, 1921, to February 1, 2019, and his pioneering work in early computing undoubtedly influenced his son's groundbreaking development of the World Wide Web.
